seoTitle: Add a DIY Arrow in Squarespace Using Shapes
metaDescription: Build a custom arrow in Squarespace with the Shape block, combining a square and diamond since there's no built-in arrow icon.
intro: Squarespace doesn't include built-in arrow icons, but you can create your own using the Shape block to guide visitors toward a call-to-action or highlight key content. This guide covers combining a square and a diamond shape to form a simple custom arrow.

steps.heading: Log in and enter edit mode
steps.body: Sign in to Squarespace, select your site, and click Edit to enter the editing interface.

steps.heading: Add a square shape for the arrow shaft
steps.body: Click Add Block, choose Shape, click the Edit icon, and select Square. Stretch it horizontally to form the arrow's shaft.

steps.heading: Add a diamond shape for the arrowhead
steps.body: Click Add Block again, choose Shape, and select Diamond from the dropdown to serve as the tip of the arrow.

steps.heading: Resize and align the shapes
steps.body: Resize and reposition the diamond so it fits naturally with the square, rotating it if needed to point in the right direction.

steps.heading: Save your custom arrow
steps.body: Once the shapes are aligned and visually balanced, click Save to publish the arrow on your page.

faq.question: Does Squarespace have a built-in arrow icon?
faq.answer: No, there's no native arrow icon, which is why combining a square and diamond shape is the standard DIY workaround.

faq.question: What can I use a custom arrow for?
faq.answer: It's useful for guiding visitors toward a call-to-action, enhancing navigation, or creating stylized section breaks.

faq.question: Can I change the color of my custom arrow?
faq.answer: Yes, both the square and diamond shapes can be styled with different colors and sizes to match your branding.

faq.question: What if my arrow doesn't line up correctly?
faq.answer: Squarespace's drag-and-drop interface makes it easy to delete and retry positioning the shapes until they align.
